title: Invoice lines in XML
prompt: The billing system exports invoices as XML, with one `<amount>` element per invoice line. Write `load(path)` so it returns each invoice's id, status, number of lines and line amounts, with the same types in every export. `export` and `solve` are written for you.
rules: Each `<invoice>` element is one row; its id is the `id` attribute. Each line is an `<amount>` element, in line order.
`lines` is how many amounts the invoice has and `line_amounts` lists them in file order, exact to the cent.
The types never change: `line_amounts` is a list even when every invoice in the file has a single line. An invoice with no lines has a missing `lines` and a missing `line_amounts`.
Return `invoice_id`, `status`, `lines` (`int`) and `line_amounts` (array of `decimal(12,2)`), in that order. A file with no invoices gives an empty result.
hints: An element that repeats inside a row is read as an array. But if no row in a file repeats it, inference reads it as a single value.
Pass a schema so the type is fixed: `amount ARRAY<DECIMAL(12,2)>`, next to `_id` and `status`.
`F.size("amount")` counts the items of an array; for a missing array it gives a missing value.
explanation: Read with `rowTag` `invoice` and the schema `_id STRING, status STRING, amount ARRAY<DECIMAL(12,2)>`, then select `_id` as `invoice_id`, `status`, `F.size("amount")` as `lines` and `amount` as `line_amounts`. The schema is what makes this safe: inference turns a repeated element into an array only when some row repeats it, so an export where every invoice has one line comes back as a single number, and it reads amounts as doubles. Declaring `amount` as a plain decimal keeps only the last line. An invoice with no `<amount>` gets a missing array, and its size is missing too.
